articleTitle: DNA-Encoded Design of Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm Fused With Whales
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: DNA coding is a branch of DNA computation, and the quality of DNA coding is an important indicator that affects the accuracy of DNA computation, and how to optimize the quality of encoding and design a better DNA coding sequence is a problem that needs to be solved, and DNA encoding optimization refers to the selection of the optimal DNA code from the DNA coding set that satisfies the constraints. In this paper, the arithmetic optimization algorithm fused with whales is used to optimize the DNA sequence. The whale strategy is used to make up for the shortcomings of some arithmetic optimization algorithms. Through the DNA sequence optimization design, the obtained results are compared with those of predecessors, and most of the experimental results are better than those of predecessors, which further illustrates the feasibility of the algorithm.

articleTitle: A Novel Evolutionary Algorithm for Multiple Traveling Salesman Problem Containing Targets with Multiple Visits
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: With the great development of economic globalization and the logistics industry, various scenarios in daily life require multiple visits to certain targets derived from the multiple traveling salesman problem. However, the research on multiple traveling salesman problems containing targets with multiple visits has not obtained enough attention, and traditional optimization algorithms have a challenge of low efficiency in solving this problem. Therefore, we propose a novel evolutionary algorithm to make it effective in solving this problem, with two novel designs on the path planning strategy and crossover operation. Finally, on the new test set generated from the classic traveling salesman problem test set Att48, we compare the proposed evolutionary algorithm with the greedy algorithm, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed evolutionary algorithm.

articleTitle: Pheromone Matrix Eigenvalue-based Convergence Assessment Indicator for Ant Colony Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: As a crucial member of the evolutionary computation (EC), ant colony optimization (ACO) converges to the optimal result through a continuous process of iterative optimization. However, determining the convergence status of an ant colony remains a challenging task without well-established methods. To this end, this paper proposes a global evaluation indicator—average absolute eigenvalue of pheromone matrix (AAEPM) by constructing a pheromone matrix and analyzing its eigenvalue variations. This indicator aims to assess the convergence status of the ant colony during the evolutionary process. Experimental results show that the AAEPM is correlated with the convergence status of ACO and is not significantly influenced by algorithm parameters and problem scale.

articleTitle: A Set-based Genetic Algorithm for Influence Maximization on Social Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Influence maximization is a crucial task of choosing a subset of users by which the number of influenced users from a social network is expected to be maximized. The IM problem is proven to be NP-hard, and it still encounters difficulties in terms of solution quality and efficiency. To cope with this problem, a set-based genetic algorithm (SGA) is proposed in this paper. In order to reduce the size of state space, the solution is encoded as a set other than a sequence, and therefore the set-based crossover and mutation operators are designed to accommodate this encoding strategy. In addition to basic arithmetic improvements, the domain of solution is further compressed by identifying potential candidates. Experiments compared the state-of-the-art algorithms on five real-world networks, and the results indicate that SGA achieves promising results in terms of solution quality and convergence speed.

articleTitle: A Performance Investigation of Genetic Algorithm with Different Evolutionary Operators
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Genetic Algorithm (GA) as a bio-inspired optimization technique, has shown significant potential for applications in many fields. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the main types of evolutionary operators in GA—selection, crossover, and mutation, which have a direct and significant influence on optimization performance. First, this study systematically summarizes the various evolutionary operators currently used in the field of GA. Subsequently, these different operators are embedded into the standard GA framework to assess their influence on algorithm performance. Last, this paper also explores the effect of setting crossover and mutation rates on GA performance, determining the optimal values of these parameters through a series of experiments. This research not only offers a comprehensive overview of the evolutionary operators in GA but also demonstrates the specific performance of different operator combinations through empirical evidence, providing valuable reference for further research and application of GA.

articleTitle: Binary Gannet Optimization Algorithm for Feature Selection Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: The Gannet Optimization Algorithm (GOA) has been proven to exhibit excellent performance in resolving issues in a range of fields. However, it is ineffective, nevertheless, when used for binary optimization issues. Therefore, this paper, aiming to further explore its outstanding capabilities, proposes for the first time using the V-shaped transfer function family to implement the binary version of the Gannet Optimization Algorithm (BGOA). Eleven datasets from the UCI Machine Learning Repository are used for feature selection applications. The transfer functions employed in BGWO-A, BPSO-T, and BQUATRE are compared with these datasets. The outcomes attest to BGOA’s exceptional performance in feature selection. It helps identify feature subsets, thereby maximizing classification accuracy while reducing feature count. This highlights the potential of the binary BGOA algorithm in exploring attributes and choosing the attributes that are most pertinent to classification issues.

articleTitle: Advancing MobileNet Security: Weighted Adversarial Learning in Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), particularly low latency models such as MobileNets have excelled in many applications, including object detection in images, speech recognition and natural language processing, but they are vulnerable to subtle perturbations that are virtually imperceptible to the human eye yet can deceive the network into misclassifying images. To enhance the robustness of such CNNs against adversaries, conventional adversarial training methods treat all data points as equally important and susceptible to attack. A weighted adversarial learning algorithm is developed in a Stackelberg game framework. This approach prioritizes data points that are more susceptible to attacks during network training. To further optimize the algorithm, we employ a Reinforcement Learning ($\mathbf{R L}$) agent to fine-tune the hyperparameters of the model, thereby increasing its robustness. Our findings indicate an increased robustness of $66.18 \%$ of the Weighted Adversary Reinforced Stackelberg Learning (WARS) against the traditional adversarial training of $64.72 \%$ in a one epoch training, using the CIFAR-10 dataset. We conclude that the WARS represents a valuable adversarial training method for bolstering the robustness of low latency CNN models.

articleTitle: Research on the Technology Architecture of Full-stack Cloud-Native Hosted Cloud
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: As cloud computing technology matures and becomes more widespread, internet-based businesses and applications of artificial intelligence become increasingly intricate. Enterprises are now more sensitive to factors such as data sensitivity, compliance requirements, and personalized needs. The surge in demand for extensive and diversified computing power is propelling the growth of the cloud hosting industry. Consequently, the expectations from cloud hosting now encompass requirements for comprehensive capabilities, security, and open compatibility. Enabling computing power, ensuring compatibility with the full-stack ecosystem, and optimizing security systems have emerged as inevitable trends in the evolution of cloud hosting services. This paper delves into the technical architecture and operational framework of full-stack cloud hosting, leveraging a range of cloud-native technologies including containers, micro-services, and DevOps. Additionally, a holistic approach to security system design is proposed to address the security challenges inherent in full-stack cloud hosting. Through tiered deployment and multi-level isolation, this approach aims to enhance the efficiency of cloud hosting business operations while providing robust security protection for cloud resources from various angles.

articleTitle: AI-Assisted Cooking Teaching System
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: This paper explores a design solution for a mobile application that combines artificial intelligence technology with traditional Chinese home cooking tutorials. The goal is to optimize the field of culinary teaching through intelligent means. We conducted a comprehensive analysis of current domestic and international approaches to integrating artificial intelligence with various domains, as well as the current development status of cooking tutorials. We pointed out that existing applications mostly lack personalized tutorials and real-time interactive guidance, making it difficult to meet the needs of personalized and immediate interaction for users. Based on these issues, the authors proposed a design solution for a personalized companion-style cooking tutorial app. This solution aims to provide more refined and personalized cooking tutorials through AI technology, as well as real-time voice interactive guidance, making the cooking process simpler and more efficient. The system adopts a frontend-backend separation architecture design, where the frontend is responsible for presenting the user interface and interaction, while the backend handles logic and data storage. In terms of functionality design, it includes not only basic features such as recipe browsing, searching, and detailed display but also specially designed modules such as voice input and AI conversation systems to enhance user interaction experience.

articleTitle: Scene Recognition Based on An Improved DenseNet with Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: High-resolution remote sensing image classification is of great significance to scene recognition and plays a pivotal role in surface cover classification, environmental monitoring, geological exploration and resource management. Convolutional neural network (CNN) has a powerful feature learning capability of automatic extraction of features and can categorize different scenes with high accuracy in scene recognition. In this study, we train on the Aerial Image Dataset (AID) and reprocess it with data augmentation. We enhance feature focus within densely connected blocks by incorporating Efficient Channel Attention (ECA), thereby proposing the ECA-DenseNet architecture. Moreover, we employ transfer learning and pre-train the network to accelerate the training process. The accuracy, precision, recall and f1 score of the final model reached ${9 7 . 1 \%, 9 7 . 0 \%, 9 6 . 8 \%}$ and ${9 6 . 9 \%}$, respectively. The experimental results show that ECA-DenseNet fully utilizes the different features extracted from each convolutional kernel and captures the key information in the scene images more effectively, which effectively improves the classification accuracy of scene recognition.

articleTitle: Crowdsourcing Logistics Scheduling Based on An Ant Colony System Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Crowdsourcing logistics has developed rapidly in recent years, in which not only the fleet of logistics companies but also occasional couriers participate in the distribution process. The new features in crowdsourcing logistics make logistics scheduling more complex. In this paper, a crowdsourcing logistics scheduling model is proposed to minimize the total distribution distance. Real-world location and traffic data crawled from Baidu Map API is incorporated into the proposed model to simulate the real-world environment. Moreover, an ant colony system approach for crowdsourcing logistics scheduling (termed ACSCLS) is proposed, which schedules the distribution routes of the fleet and couriers. A real-world dataset of Guangzhou, China is constructed, including eight instances. Experimental results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed ACS-CLS approach.

articleTitle: Adapted Genetic Algorithm for Orienteering Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: The Orienteering Problem (OP) is a well-known route optimization problem with various real-world applications. It aims at finding the most valuable path by visiting a set of nodes within a given path length limit. It involves both the node selection and the path optimization and thus is difficult to solve. Genetic algorithm (GA) is known for its effectiveness in solving combinatorial optimization problems. Inspired from this, this paper adapts the genetic algorithm to solve OP mainly by adapting the crossover operation. To this end, this paper adapts seven popular crossover operations, namely position-based crossover based on order selection (OSPBX), position-based crossover based on greedy selection (GSPBX), order crossover based on order selection (OSOX), order crossover based on greedy selection (GSOX), partially mapped crossover (PMX), heuristic crossover (HX), and sequential constructed crossover (SCX). To further improve the quality of the obtained solution, this paper first leverages the 2-opt method to fine-tune the path and then further devises a vertex insertion method to additionally add more nodes in the fine-tuned path when its travelling length is within the given limit. Experiments have been conducted on various OP instances from small-scale to large-scale to investigate the effectiveness of the adapted GA with the seven crossover operators. The experimental results reveal that the adapted GA with seven crossover operators are very promising for solving OP.

articleTitle: Rumor Detection by Jointly Learning Propagation Patterns and Users’ Personas
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Information spreads rapidly on social media these days, regardless of its facticity. Consequently, rumor detection has become a critical task. Existing methods have focused on analyzing the content of source claim or the propagation graph formed by responsive posts. However, few studies delve into generating valid representations for users’ personas, which have been shown of great importance according to the journalism and communication research. In this paper, we propose a rumor detection model named $JoPU$ that jointly learns propagation patterns and users’ personas. Generally, our JoPU model is realized by bi-level graph learning. First, users are characterized by their profiles and historical posts, forming a relation graph. Micro-level graph learning is then employed to generate users’ personas representations. Second, on the information propagation graph, we fuse the text features of responsive posts and the learned users’ personas, and then perform macro-level graph learning. Finally, the network is trained in a multi-task way, incorporating the downstream task of rumor detection and an auxiliary task of user similarity, with adaptive tuning of the two tasks weights. Experimental results demonstrate that our model outperform state-of-the-art models.

articleTitle: Can Individuals be Repeatedly Selected for Mutation in Matrix-Based DE? A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Evolutionary Computation (EC) is a class of algorithms derived from the simulation of natural phenomena, which faces the challenges of long running times and high computing loads resulting from large-scale problems. For this reason, the matrix-based EC (MEC) has been presented as an extension of classic EC algorithms to address large-scale optimization. The MEC can be implemented directly on high-performance computing resources, thus accelerating the computation of evolutionary operators. However, MEC is still in its infancy and lacks deeper analysis. Hence, this paper analyzes and investigates matrix-based differential evolution (MDE) and advances the development of related research through theoretical analysis and experimental validation, which has two contributions. First, through the comprehensive comparison of MDE and DE in different problems, we compare the solution quality and computational speed of MDE and DE, and show that the solution quality of MDE is not significantly different from that of DE, but the computational speed of MDE is much faster than that of DE. Second, we also further analyze the mutation mechanism of MDE, focusing on the effect of the repeatability of individuals in the mutation process on the performance of the algorithms, which provides a basis for future research on MDE of MEC.

articleTitle: Voiceprint Challenge for Cryptographic Authentication Based on Triplet Networks and Fuzzy Extractors
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Due to its uniqueness and readiness availability, biometric information has been widely used for secure authentication in various contexts, such as user authentication, authorized access, and online payments. However, biometric information involves personal privacy, and the potential leakage of biometric information is extremely harmful. At present, most of the methods that use biometric information for authentication, such as fuzzy extractors, only protect the template, but cannot resist biometric information replay attacks. This paper proposes a voiceprint challenge-based cryptographic authentication framework (VCCAF), which integrates the user’s ownership of the terminal device into one-time voiceprint challenge to overcome possible biometric information replay attacks. The one-time voiceprint challenge constructs a text content with voiceprint information removed through secure multi-party computation, thus avoiding the possible leakage of the raw sound data due to network transmission. Moreover, a time-delay neural network (TDNN)-based triplet network is employed to extract voiceprint features, and then a reusable fuzzy extractor is applied to complete the challenge by passing the local voiceprint check. The experimental results show that the proposed framework supports incremental registration of users with excellent scalability, and provides a promising cryptographic authentication paradigm for practical authorized access applications.

articleTitle: Collision-Aware Evolutionary Algorithm for Multi-Agent Coverage Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Multi-agent coverage path planning (MACPP) aims to find the shortest paths for agents to collaboratively accomplish an area coverage task. Most current MACPP studies focus on introducing various area decomposition methods to decouple the MACPP problem into individual single-agent path planning problem. However, these methods often neglect the collisions among agents in the planning process, which may result in agent crashes. In this paper, we introduce a collision-aware evolutionary algorithm to provide a collision-free path set for agents. The proposed algorithm adopts the trapezoidal decomposition to divide the region into convex areas and evenly assigns these areas to agents. Based on the decomposed areas, we propose an interarea visiting order planning method for agents. Within each area, we implement intra-area coverage path planning for each agent. Furthermore, we incorporate collision detection between agents and adjust the paths of conflict agents to prevent collisions. Finally, we conduct experiments with three state-of-the-art approaches in four different environments to verify that the proposed algorithm can effectively complete the task and avoid the collision risk.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Heuristic Set-based Particle Swarm Optimizer for the Multi-Objective Task Assigning Problem in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: The task assigning problem in wireless sensor networks is a challenging NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem that has caught much attention. Although binary particle swarm optimizers have been proven to be effective for this problem, the prematurity remains severe. To fix the prematurity, this paper proposes a set-based particle swarm optimizer with dynamic heuristic substitution techniques. Differing from the original binary particle swarm optimizer, the representation scheme is based on the concept of set. The position of each particle is a set whose elements are defined by the problem. A particle position element denotes the allocation of a task to a sensor node. The proposed algorithm tries to select an optimal subset from the universal set based on the particle swarm optimization framework. Moreover, the comprehensive learning strategy that utilizes beneficial information from the best-ever positions of all particles is employed, which helps keep the swarm away from local optima. Considering the constraints in real-world situations, the position updating adopts a substitution operation, guided by heuristic information that dynamically alters. To improve particle diversity, mutation operations are carried out after renewing the particle positions. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed approach over others.

articleTitle: Orthogonal Design Assisted Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved orthogonal design assisted particle swarm optimization (ODPSO), effectively addressing the issue of traditional PSO easily getting trapped in local optima. Constructed using the orthogonal experimental design method, the orthogonal table of ODPSO integrates information from the current position of particles, individual best positions, and global best positions, enhancing global search capabilities while reducing reliance on random initial particles, thereby avoiding premature convergence, and strengthening optimization capabilities. Across 13 benchmark functions in the continuous domain, ODPSO demonstrates faster convergence speed and higher optimization accuracy compared to traditional particle swarm optimization (PSO), orthogonal predicted genetic algorithm (OPGA), and other algorithms, particularly excelling in multimodal functions. The innovation of this study lies in proposing a novel orthogonal learning strategy and demonstrating the effectiveness of ODPSO through systematic evaluation, providing robust support for the improvement of PSO.

articleTitle: A Novel Three-Phase Feature Selection Algorithm for Major Depressive Disorder Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Except for the “curse of dimensionality”, the challenge of inaccurate class labels is introduced in the high-dimensional feature selection (FS) problem in the realm of major depressive disorder (MDD) auxiliary diagnosis. This article proposed a novel three-phase FS algorithm, named aTPFS, for MDD classification using resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (R-fMRI) to address the above two challenges concurrently. aTPFS integrates relevance-guided clustering (Phase One and Phase Two) and a genetic algorithm (Phase Three). In the first two phases, features are sorted by their relevance and divided into feature clusters with low computational costs. After that, diverse representative feature subsets are generated for application across different samples, using an evolutionary algorithm in Phase Three. The efficacy of the proposed algorithm was verified on the multi-site REST-meta-MDD dataset in comparison with statistical $\boldsymbol{t}$-test and two partial aTPFS. Experimental results showcase the ability to handle sample diversity through the extraction of feature subsets from feature clusters. Nevertheless, further modifications to the genetic algorithm are warranted to enhance MDD classification accuracy in the future.

articleTitle: Decoding Domain-Specific NER: A Performance Evaluation of ChatGPT, Bi-LSTM, and BERT
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Named Entity Recognition (NER) is a vital method in natural language processing (NLP), extracting information by identifying and categorizing entities in textual data. This study delves into the dynamic landscape of NER models, considering recent advances in transfer learning with transformers like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and large language models such as ChatGPT. We evaluate and compare their performances on a custom domain-specific and limited corpus. Utilizing state-of-the-art techniques, we model multi-layered prompts for ChatGPT, concurrently utilizing the Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Networks (Bi-LSTM) model and fine-tuning a pre-trained BERT model for NER on the corpus. Our study offers crucial insights into these models’ viability under constrained, domain-specific dataset conditions, given the effectiveness of transfer learning and zeroshot classification with large language models. Our experimental results highlight that Bi-LSTM excels over ChatGPT and finetuned BERT on the custom dataset, with the added benefit of faster training times. We emphasize the importance of considering domain and task-specific factors and corpus size when selecting a model.

articleTitle: Surrogate-Assisted Level-Based Learning Particle Swarm Optimizer Based on Expected Value Evaluation under High Noise Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithms (SAEAs) have emerged as an effective approach for addressing expensive optimization problems. However, in scenarios where uncertain factors such as evaluation noises exist, the performance and reliability of most SAEAs are compromised due to inaccuracies and uncertainties, such as biases and measurement errors, which may vary. To mitigate these challenges, this paper proposes a particle re-evaluation technique based on a classifier-assisted approach. Specifically, the technique leverages a classifier-assisted level-based learning swarm optimizer to enhance the algorithm’s performance and reliability. Moreover, it explores various reevaluation rules tailored for uncertain conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that re-evaluation significantly enhances the classifier-assisted level-based learning swarm optimizers’ ability to improve performance and reliability, particularly in environments where objective fitness is sensitive to disturbances. Additionally, the experiments show that re-evaluation substantially boosts the optimizers’ capacity to discover superior solutions and enhances particle trustworthiness in uncertain situations.

articleTitle: A new decomposition method for fully non-separable large-scale problem
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Large-scale global optimization (LSGO) problem is such a problem containing hundreds or thousands of decision variables. Solving LSGO problems is very challenging due to its high nonlinearity, high dimensionality and too many local optimal solutions. LSGO algorithms typically employ a divide-and-conquer strategy to solve the problem. This involves decomposing the LSGO problem into subproblems and solving them individually. The most challenging LSGO problems are those that cannot be divided due to interactions between variables. We propose a decomposition method to divide variables of fully non-separable LSGO problems into sub groups in a reasonable way. We design a hybrid decomposition scheme by integrating four decomposition strategies so as to get better decomposition result. Numerical experimental results show that the proposed decomposition method is effective and totally outperforms the correct decomposition (non-decomposition).

articleTitle: Multi-Strategy Fusion Enhanced Dung Beetle Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an Enhanced Distributed Blackout Optimization (EDBO) algorithm, which is an improved metaheuristic based on the original Distributed Blackout Optimization (DBO). The EDBO addresses the limitations of the DBO, such as insufficient global exploration, low convergence accuracy, and a tendency to converge to local optima. The EDBO incorporates multiple strategies to enhance its performance. Initially, a novel spiral exploration strategy is employed to replace the original reproduction phase of the DBO, facilitating the algorithm’s ability to escape local optima. Subsequently, an optimal value guidance strategy is introduced during the foraging phase to balance exploration and exploitation. Furthermore, a lens imaging-based reverse learning strategy is utilized to expand the search space and increase population diversity. Experimental results on the CEC2017 test suite demonstrate the efficacy of the EDBO, showing significant improvements in optimization performance and search precision compared to the traditional DBO and other state-of-the-art algorithms. These results validate the effectiveness of the proposed EDBO algorithm.

articleTitle: Hilbert-encoded Cooperative Coevolutionary Genetic Algorithm for Few-shot Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: In recent years, the advancement of artificial intelligence algorithms, particularly in the domain of semantic segmentation within computer vision, has been noteworthy. This progress is attributed to the availability of diverse large-scale datasets and the continual improvement of computational resources, with deep learning serving as a representative paradigm. Consequently, numerous sophisticated segmentation models have emerged for visual tasks. However, the efficacy of these models hinges on the availability of substantial annotated datasets for training. A notable challenge arises in scenarios where few-shot datasets are prevalent due to inherent limitations. The sparse data volume in these instances often stems from difficulties in obtaining a sufficiently large and high-quality dataset. The process of image annotation is resource-intensive, demanding considerable time and human effort. Addressing the consequential shortage of sample size in few-shot datasets becomes a paramount concern. This paper tackles the aforementioned issues related to few-shot datasets and introduces the Hilbert encoded cooperative coevolutionary genetic algorithm (HCCGA), a novel image enhancement algorithm designed for the automated generation of 3D-Lookup Tables (3D LUTs). HCCGA leverages 3D LUTs generated automatically through the genetic algorithm to map the original few-shot dataset, thereby obtaining a more extensive set of high-quality samples. The methodology employed in this research encompasses the generation and optimization of 3D LUTs using a divide-and-conquer strategy based on genetic algorithms. Additionally, it involves the mapping of new images using 3D LUTs in conjunction with sampling and interpolation. The evaluation of the proposed approach encompasses comparisons based on various image binary classification evaluation metrics applied to images before and after mapping through the results of model inference. Experimental results obtained using HCCGA on diverse public datasets, combined with state-of-the-art segmentation models, demonstrate the superiority of the optimized 3D-LUTs-mapped samples over their unmapped counterparts. This superiority is evident in terms of various standard evaluation metrics, including precision, recall, and F1score. Furthermore, the high-quality images generated by this method offer a viable solution to augment the original dataset, effectively addressing the significant inadequacy in the number of samples within few-shot datasets.

articleTitle: Securing UAV Delivery Systems with Blockchain and Large Language Models: An Innovative Logistics Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: In the evolving landscape of logistics and supply chain management, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have emerged as a promising solution to enhance delivery efficiency and reach. However, the integration of UAVs into mainstream logistics faces significant challenges, including security, data integrity, and scalable customer interaction. This study proposes an innovative framework that leverages blockchain technology and large language models to address these challenges, offering a secure, transparent, and intelligent UAV delivery system. By integrating blockchain, we ensure the immutability and transparency of delivery transactions, enhancing trust in UAV-operated logistics. Concurrently, the employment of large language models facilitates intelligent route optimization, dynamic task allocation, and real-time customer service through natural language processing capabilities. We present a comprehensive analysis of the proposed system’s architecture, security features, and operational efficiency through simulated delivery scenarios. Our findings indicate a notable improvement in delivery times, reduced operational costs, and enhanced customer satisfaction. This research not only contributes to the theoretical understanding of blockchain and AI applications in logistics but also provides a practical roadmap for implementing secure and efficient UAV delivery systems in the future.

articleTitle: Ant Colony Optimization for Multiple Traveling Salesmen Problem with Revisitable Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Multiple traveling salesmen problem (MTSP) is a widespread combinatorial optimization problem that aims to minimize the total cost of all salesmen. MTSP with revisitable cities (MTSPR) is an extension of MTSP, which considers the possibility of visiting specific cities multiple times, making it more applicable to real-world scenarios. To address the issue, this paper presents a novel ant colony optimization for MTSPR (RACO), efficiently solving MTSPR with a novel path construction strategy. Specifically, first, the problem definition of the MTSPR is presented, followed by the mathematical formulation of its constraints and optimization objectives. Then, a collaborative balanced path selection strategy is proposed, which constructs paths for all salesmen through balanced control and parallel selection to achieve efficient path construction. In addition, a 2-opt local search strategy is employed to enhance the path optimization of elite ants. Finally, experiments on TSPLIB benchmark sets show that RACO has better performance than other state-of-art algorithms in solving MTSPR.

articleTitle: An Ant Colony System Algorithm for Multiple Traveling Salesman Problem with Hub Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Logistics serves as the bridge for commodities to flow from production sites to consumption sites, which is important to industrial development and economic growth. Efficient organization of logistics scheduling can reduce the costs of production and sales of commodities. Logistics scheduling can be modeled as a multiple traveling salesman problem (MTSP). Traditional MTSPs do not take the different business requirements of cities into account, resulting in potentially large disparities in the amount of business for each traveling salesman. In this paper, we focus on the scenario where some cities have high requirements for commodities and thus they should be visited by multiple traveling salesmen. Such cities are termed hub cities. The objective of the scenario is to minimize the sum of the path lengths of multiple traveling salesmen and to make the difference between the path lengths of the multiple traveling salesmen as small as possible. To address the above problem, we propose an ACS-MTSP algorithm. The ACS-MTSP selects the next city to be visited alternately by multiple traveling salesmen, and the construction of the path is completed when all cities have been visited. In order to minimize the difference between the path lengths of the multiple traveling salesmen, the current path lengths of the multiple traveling salesmen are taken into account when selecting the next city to visit. Experimental results for different MTSP instances with different numbers of cities and hub cities show that the ACS-MTSP is effective in reducing traveling salesmen costs.

articleTitle: LASE: A Forward-Looking Item Selection Strategy for CD-CAT
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Cognitive diagnostic computerized adaptive testing (CD-CAT) is a cutting-edge testing approach in educational environments. It combines the merits of computerized adaptive testing (CAT) and cognitive diagnosis models (CDMs), allowing for adaptive testing methods to be applied to fine-grained diagnosis. Two crucial factors in CD-CAT item selection are diagnostic accuracy and item bank utilization. Previous research focused either solely on enhancing diagnostic performance or on achieving a balance between bank utilization and diagnostic accuracy, often at the significant expense of the latter. To strike a more effective equilibrium between diagnostic performance and bank utilization, the current study proposes a forwardlooking item selection strategy for CD-CAT, named lookingahead Shannon entropy (LASE). LASE shifts the focus from the immediate next item to a broader perspective, considering sequences of multiple items ahead, thereby offering a longer-term view in item selection. This strategy involves a branch searching scheme to find appropriate multi-item sequences and introduces the LASE metric for evaluating these sequences. The parameter within the LASE method are investigated. Simulation studies based on two item banks are conducted to demonstrate LASE’s effectiveness compared to existing methods. The results show that LASE offers a more balanced item selection for CD-CAT in terms of diagnostic accuracy and bank utilization.

articleTitle: Improving Speech Emotion Recognition with Dynamic Features and Temporal Correlations
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: As a core content of human-computer interaction, Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) is receiving increasing attention and emphasis. However, recent deep learning-based recognition models typically utilize Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to extract acoustic features, while ignoring the emotional information in the time series, which can capture the dynamic changes in speech signals. To address the aforementioned issue, we propose a novel speech emotion recognition model based on Dynamic Feature learning and Temporal Correlation encoding, namely SERDFTC. To be specific, we design a emotion-related temporal correlations (ETC) module, which introduces Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BLSTM) to capture of the temporal characteristics of speech signals. Moreover, ETC introduces the attention module to enhance the model’s ability to focus on the key components of the speech signals. By embedding ETC module, our SER-DFTC can effectively capture the dynamic changes in speech signals and encode the rich temporal correlation information, thereby improving the final recognition accuracy and robustness. In addition, we improve the static feature extraction method, Mel spectrogram, by fusing its first and second-order differences to form three-channel log Mel-spectrograms (3-ch log Mel-spec), which can better reflect the dynamic characteristics of speech signals and are more suitable for the training of SER network. Experimental results on three classic datasets show that the proposed improved feature extraction model effectively improves the performance of speech emotion recognition.

articleTitle: Adapted Ant Colony Optimization for Team Orienteering Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: The Team Orienteering Problem (TOP) is to find multiple optimal subsets of nodes and the associated routes to visit these nodes with the objective to maximize the total profits and under the constraint that the traveling cost of each route does not exceed the given cost limit. Such a problem is very challenging and difficult to solve because it involves node selection optimization, route optimization, and cost constraints for multiple routes. Thanks to the significantly good performance of Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithms in solving path planning problems, they are considered promising for addressing TOP. To this end, this paper takes the first attempt to adapt five classical ACO algorithms, namely the Ant System (AS), Elitist Ant System (EAS), Rank-based Ant System (AS rank), Min-Max Ant System (MMAS), and Ant Colony System (ACS), to solve TOP. To achieve this, we maintain an ant team consisting of multiple ants to construct a feasible solution containing multiple routes. Further, we design an ant selection scheme for the ant team to select the next node to visit in the route construction by considering the given cost constraints. To assess the optimization performance of the five adapted ACO algorithms in solving TOP, experiments are conducted on the classical TOP instances. The results reveal that all five ACO algorithms are promising for addressing TOP. Particularly, ACS excels in maximizing the overall team profit, while EAS demonstrates good stability in minimizing the profit differences between routes.

articleTitle: Population-Level Hybridization between Roulette Wheel Selection and Tournament Selection for Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: This paper introduces a population-level hybrid selection framework that combines the roulette wheel selection (RWS) and the tournament selection (TS) to pick promising exemplars to update particles, so as to ameliorate the capability of particle swarm optimization (PSO). As a result, a novel PSO, named PLHPSO is developed. PLHPSO distinguishes itself from the conventional PSO by employing a variety of exemplar selection strategies to steer the update of particles. To be precise, this framework first selects two different exemplars from all personally best positions and then it compares the particle to be updated with the two chosen exemplars. Next, different update strategies are designed to update the particle based on the comparison results. Subsequently, under this framework, totally six selection methods are developed, including TS, RWS, and their four hybridizations. With these selection strategies, particles in PLHPSO are able to learn from a wide range of directional exemplars, and hence the updating diversity of the swarm is hopefully increased. Experiments on the 50-D and 100-D CEC2014 benchmark problem suites demonstrate that PLHPSO with the six selection strategies outperform the traditional global and local PSOs. Particularly, among the six selection methods, the linearly decreasing hybridization between RWS and TS stands out as the most helpful one for PLHPSO to cope with optimization problems effectively.

articleTitle: Benchmark for Multiple Traveling Salesmen Problem with Visiting Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Multiple Traveling Salesmen Problem with Visiting Constraints (VCMTSP) is a universal variant of Multiple Traveling Salesmen Problem (MTSP) by modeling the accessibility of salesmen to cities with a general accessibility matrix. Such a problem widely exists in practice and has attracted attentions from researchers. However, as far as we know, there is no common benchmark set in VCMTSP for researchers to evaluate the optimization effectiveness of their optimization methods. To fill this gap, this paper builds a common VCMTSP benchmark set based on the popular TSPLIB set. In particular, this benchmark set consists of VCMTSP instances with a variety of numbers of salesmen and cities along with three different types of visiting constraints, namely tight visiting constraints, moderate visiting constraints, and loose visiting constraints. To assess the validity of this benchmark set, this paper further adapts two classical evolutionary algorithms, namely Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA), to tackle the established VCMTSP instances. Experimental results show that GA and ACO are capable of addressing VCMTSP, yet their performance still needs improvement. With this study, it is expected that the established VCMTSP instances could provide a benchmark set for researchers to comprehensively validate their optimization methods by fairly comparing with others in this direction. In particular, the benchmark set can be accessed by https://gitee.com/absinthhh/vcmtsp.

articleTitle: Parallel Multi-stages Rectification Networks for 3D Skeleton-based Motion Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: The recursive neural network, commonly utilized in human prediction tasks, demonstrates an intrinsic proclivity for error accumulation. We designed a three-stage parallel prediction network, which guides the output generation of these three networks with different objectives. Then, we use the high-dimensional information in these three networks to fuse new information to generate the final output. In addition, we also designed a fusion block based on GRU and attention mechanism to extract high-dimensional information more efficiently. Our method has proven to be more effective than most recent techniques in forecasting movement over short and long timeframes in Human 3.6M and CMU Mocap datasets, as evidenced by extensive testing.

articleTitle: A Variation-Based Genetic Algorithm for Privacy-Preserving Data Publishing
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Facing the escalating need for data sharing against the backdrop of stringent privacy demands, this study shows Variation-Based Genetic Algorithm (VB-GA) aimed at navigating the complexities of balancing privacy and utility in privacy-preserving data publishing. By integrating attribute generalisation and record suppression, VB-GA proposes a refined strategy for anonymization. It further incorporates specially designed crossover and mutation operators to optimise information exchange and enhance the anonymization process. Comprehensive experimental analysis reveals VB-GA’s ability to improve solution accuracy and hasten convergence, underscoring its efficiency in balancing privacy preservation with data utility. This research represents a pivotal advancement in data management practices amidst growing privacy valuation, highlighting genetic algorithms’ potential to refine privacy-preserving data publishing and ensure a judicious data governance approach. It delineates a pathway towards reconciling the intricate challenge of safeguarding data privacy without undermining its inherent value, setting a new standard for addressing privacy concerns in the digital age.

articleTitle: A Multiobjective Ant Colony System for Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: Multi-agent pickup and delivery (MAPD) holds great significance in practical logistics and distribution systems. This paper models the problem as a multiobjective problem, wherein a group of heterogeneous agents collaboratively performs pickup and delivery tasks to minimize the working time and achieve workload balance among agents. Consider two realistic constraints: first, the total workload of each agent must not exceed its maximum load capacity; second, the pickup task must be executed before the delivery one. To tackle this issue, we propose a multiobjective ant colony system (MOACS), employing a single colony and two pheromone matrices to optimize both objectives simultaneously. One pheromone matrix records the historical experience on optimizing the working time, and the other records searching information on maintaining workload balance. Each ant adopts a different parameter to combine the pheromone values from two matrices, so as to explore different subareas. Besides, a probabilistic equilibrium selection strategy is designed to further balance the optimization between objectives and improve solution quality. Experimental findings over a wide range of instance scales demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed MOACS over three established ACS-based multiobjective algorithms.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cross-Community Diffusion Through Swarm Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: The proliferation of information online reveals a discernible pattern: a social information barrier named “information cocoons.” Within these cocoons, individuals are inclined to engage exclusively with and focus on information sources aligning with their pre-existing views, predisposing them to neglect or dismiss contrary information. Aiming to address this issue, this paper extends the existing Information Maximization problem by incorporating network community information. It formulates a cross-community communication maximization problem and proposes effective solutions, encompassing the following key elements. Firstly, a cross-community communication effect evaluation index is introduced based on diversity entropy, to address the challenge of unclear criteria for evaluating cross-community communication effects. This index is designed to assess the diversity of information in cross-community communication. Then, employing linear weighting, the multi-objective communication optimization problem related to cross-community communication is transformed into a single-objective optimization problem. Various heuristic and meta-heuristic methods are employed to solve such problems. Through simulation experiments, the efficiency and solution quality of different methods are evaluated. This empirical approach serves to validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods in diverse scenarios.

articleTitle: Competition-Based Stochastic Learning Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm for Large-Scale Optimization Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Machine Intelligence Theory and Applications (MiTA)
abstract: With the development of information technology, large-scale optimization problem is the core issue in various applications. Due to the high dimension characteristics, large-scale optimization problems are challenging to solve. Therefore, this paper proposes a competition-based stochastic learning particle swarm optimization algorithm (CSLPSO) for solving large-scale optimization problems efficiently, which has two novel designs. First, a competition-based stochastic learning strategy is proposed to improve the exploration ability of PSO. Second, a parameter control mechanism suitable for the CSLPSO algorithm is proposed, so that the algorithm does not require manual parameter selection. In the experiment, the CSLPSO algorithm is applied to 12 large-scale problems with state-of-the-art algorithms as competitors. The experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed CSLPSO.
